assessment: The original 2017 EAACI PDS book contains Yang et al. 0275, which compares reported food reactions and allergy sensitization in urban and rural schoolchildren and tests shrimp, mite and cockroach allergen cross-reactivity in a laboratory subset. Other shrimp abstracts concern allergy cross-reactivity or immunotherapy. The separate Parkinson mention in the antibiotic prophylaxis trial is a recorded death, not a shrimp comparison or a falls outcome.

assessment: Namork et al. 0573 used acetone and olive oil as a topical mouse vehicle for contact-allergen sensitization. Leong et al. 0436 included olive oil among yeast culture-medium additives for dermatology research. Dysphagia was reported in separate allergy and eosinophilic oesophagitis contexts. The book gives no edible extra-virgin olive-oil comparison for Parkinson swallowing.
